issues.description: The return type for retrieving all persons is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and client expect a List<Person> from GET /persons (problem states the persons are returned as a list and the client-side PersonController deserializes to List<Person>), the template's PersonService.getAllPersons declares and returns a List<Person>, but the solution's PersonService.getAllPersons returns a Set<Person>. Meanwhile PersonResource in the solution declares ResponseEntity<List<Person>> but forwards the call to the service method that returns a Set. This mismatch breaks type consistency between server and client and will cause compilation or runtime issues and confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the service, resource and client agree on the same collection type. The simplest fix is to change PersonService.getAllPersons to return a List<Person> (matching the problem statement and client). Implement sorting on a List and return e.g. Collections.unmodifiableList(sortedList) or new ArrayList<>(sortedList). Ensure PersonResource forwards that List and the client deserializes to List<Person> as currently implemented.
